title: Speech and Audio Processing
tagline: Speech and audio, from the physics of a sound to the models that understand it.
intro: Interactive notes built for the classroom. Each page starts from intuition and everyday analogies, then adds the maths, figures, listening examples and live demos that run in your browser. New modules are added as the course grows.

modules.title: Seeing sound: the spectrogram
modules.summary: How a spectrogram is computed and inverted (STFT, windows, overlap-add), wideband vs narrowband views, why decibels and colour maps matter, and how to read harmonics, formants and noise bursts as phonemes.
modules.short: STFT, windows and resolution; reading harmonics, formants and noise in real speech.
learn: How the STFT turns a waveform into a picture, and back again
Wideband vs narrowband, decibels and colour maps
Reading vowels, fricatives, stops and nasals

modules.title: The sounds of language
modules.summary: From sound to phoneme: phones, minimal pairs and allophones (with real Indian-English recordings), how consonants and vowels are classified, the IPA and distinctive features, and how English and Hindi differ. Then phoneme inventories of the world and of India from PHOIBLE 2.0 and Glottolog, with a live explorer.
modules.short: Phonemes, minimal pairs and allophones; how speech sounds are classified, and the IPA.

pages.title: The sounds of language: from sound to phoneme
Phoneme inventories: India and the world

learn: From sound to phoneme: minimal pairs and allophones
Classifying sounds: place, manner, voicing; vowel height and backness
How India's inventories compare with the world's, explored live

modules.title: A buzz and a tube: the source–filter model
modules.summary: Speech production built up from analogies: struck slabs and impulse responses, a spring–mass resonator, tubes and their resonances, formants, vocal-tract length, and the vowel space.
modules.short: How speech is made: a vocal-fold source shaped by the resonances of the vocal tract.
learn: Impulse responses and resonance from everyday analogies
Glottal pulses, harmonics and the vowel space

modules.title: Guessing the next sample: correlation, prediction and AR models
modules.summary: From the scatter of neighbouring samples to linear prediction; estimating the coefficients; the residual; and how Yule and Walker invented the method on sunspot records, retold with their data and with real speech.
modules.short: Correlation, linear prediction and AR models, from sunspots to speech.
learn: How sunspot records led to linear prediction

modules.title: Linear prediction for speech
modules.summary: The predictor as an all-pole vocal tract: poles and formants, the LPC envelope, analysis and resynthesis, and modifying pitch and voice with playback demos.
modules.short: The all-pole vocal tract: formants, LPC envelopes, analysis and resynthesis.
learn: Poles as formants: the all-pole vocal tract
LPC envelopes and choosing the order

modules.title: Speech codecs
modules.summary: Squeezing speech through a wire: quantisation and sampling, μ-law, predictive coding (ADPCM) and the LPC vocoder, with listening examples at real bit rates.
modules.short: Squeezing speech into bits: quantisation, μ-law, ADPCM and the LPC vocoder.
learn: Predictive coding: send only the surprise (ADPCM)
The LPC vocoder: send the model, not the waveform

extras.title: Toolbox
extras.summary: Background ideas that the modules lean on.

pages.title: Why does audio live in decibels?
pages.blurb: Why audio is measured in dB: the ear, spectra and errors.

pages.title: Convolution, animated
pages.blurb: Convolution animated, and room reverberation as a convolution.

updates.text: Module 2 now opens with phonemes, minimal pairs, allophones and distinctive features.
Site launched: modules 1–6 and the toolbox. New page on the spectrogram. All speech examples use the CMU ARCTIC ksp voice (Indian English) and an Indian-English recording.

howto: Use headphones: most pages have listening examples.
A laptop or desktop works best for the live demos; everything also reads on a phone.
Each page follows the same rhythm: intuition, then maths, figures and demos, then questions to check yourself.
